reconcile.note: Matthew Henry explains the two named sons in Chronicles 29 as zealous volunteers singled out for a task, not an exhaustive list of Heman's fourteen sons.

discrepancy.note: Wellhausen argues the fourteen names in 1 Chronicles 25:4 are not real sons at all but fragments of a Hebrew sentence broken into a name list.

quotes.text: The names of the six Levitical classes according to 1Chronicles xxv. 4, Giddalti, V'romamti-Ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, Mahazioth, are simply the fragments of a consecutive sentence which runs: I have magnified | and exalted the help | of him who sat in need: | I have spoken | abundance of | prophecies.
quotes.attr: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel, trans. Black & Menzies (1885), ch. on the Levites under David, on 1 Chronicles 25:4.
